issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub-nsf-stemed-stretch/brief.md: “we can adapt the annotation scheme for math problem-solving responses”; task.yaml T2 “type: T07” and “plan to develop or collect new math-specific data from the target population”.
issues.problem: The brief proposes adaptation of an annotation scheme; it does not claim a planned child-math dataset already exists. Such adaptation is compatible with the call’s requirement to justify measures for the target learners. The key turns a legitimate suggestion into a categorical prohibition and forces new data development/collection even though an applicant could validate an adapted scheme, use an appropriate available instrument/dataset with prospective permission, or choose another sound design. No actual T07 planned-as-existing claim is planted, so this trap is unfair as written.
issues.fix: Delete T2 from task.yaml and retain the annotation-adaptation idea as ordinary scientific guidance. One trap is permitted; do not manufacture a replacement merely to retain the count. Assess measure validity through the call’s existing SC3 and scientific-quality items. If future authoring adds a genuine T07 trap, it must first plant an explicit, realistic claim that a currently absent resource is already in hand and accept any feasible route to obtain/validate the needed evidence.
